record.oneLiner: An Early Jurassic sauropodomorph, one of the first dinosaurs named.
record.description: Massospondylus was an early sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic of southern Africa and one of the best-known of its group. Described by Richard Owen in 1854, it was among the first dinosaurs ever named. It is known from abundant specimens, including embryos preserved in eggs.

notableFacts.text: One of the first dinosaurs ever named (Owen, 1854).
Known from abundant specimens, including embryos inside eggs.
Owen named it 'longer vertebra' from bones he thought were from the tail — now known to be from the neck.
